prompt:
We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Research what the Home Assistant project has officially published about the number of active installations (its opt-in analytics). Cite the page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Below is what I found in the web search results you provided. I have not done additional browsing beyond those results.

SOURCE: https://analytics.home-assistant.io/ | QUOTE: "695,026 Active Home Assistant Installations" | CLAIM: This is the current count shown on the official Home Assistant Analytics dashboard for active installations that are part of the opt-in analytics system.

SOURCE: https://analytics.home-assistant.io/statistics/ | QUOTE: "496,813 of 637,194 (77.97%) installations have chosen to share usage statistics" | CLAIM: This shows both the subset of analytics-participating installations that share usage statistics and the larger active-installation count it is drawn from.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/analytics | QUOTE: "Analytics in Home Assistant are opt-in and do not reflect the entire Home Assistant userbase." | CLAIM: The published analytics installation count should not be interpreted as the total number of Home Assistant users or installations.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/analytics | QUOTE: "We estimate that less than a fourth of all Home Assistant users opt in." | CLAIM: Home Assistant officially says the analytics-visible installations are a minority of the real userbase, estimated at under 25%.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/analytics | QUOTE: "The Analytics system was introduced in Home Assistant 2021.4, and it's used by 76.5% of the active installations." | CLAIM: Within the set of active installations known to the analytics system, most have enabled analytics.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2021/11/12/100k-analytics/ | QUOTE: "Today we have reached a major milestone for Home Assistant Analytics: 100,000 users have opted in to be included!" | CLAIM: Home Assistant officially announced that opt-in analytics participation had reached 100,000 at that time.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2021/11/12/100k-analytics/ | QUOTE: "The 100,000 installations are not the total number of Home Assistant users." | CLAIM: The project explicitly warned that the analytics milestone was not a total user count.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2021/11/12/100k-analytics/ | QUOTE: "The truth here is that we don’t know the total number of installations because Home Assistant is private by design." | CLAIM: Home Assistant has officially said it cannot know the total number of installations.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2021/11/12/100k-analytics/ | QUOTE: "Our estimate is that there are 4-5x more installations than people that opt-in to analytics." | CLAIM: Home Assistant's public estimate at that time was that total installations were roughly 4 to 5 times the opt-in analytics count.

SOURCE: https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2025/04/16/state-of-the-open-home-recap/ | QUOTE: "One big announcement Franck made was that this year we went from 1 million to over 2 million active installations in 2024!" | CLAIM: In an official 2025 recap, Home Assistant stated that active installations grew from 1 million to over 2 million in 2024.

One important note: the analytics dashboard count and the 2025 recap count appear to be talking about different things. The analytics pages are explicitly tied to opt-in analytics, while the 2025 recap is describing a broader active-installation estimate. Based on the quotes above, you should not treat the analytics number as the full installed base.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: a current official Home Assistant page stating the total number of all Home Assistant installations, not just the opt-in analytics count

Uncertain:
- I only used the search results provided to me, so I cannot verify whether the dashboard has changed since those results were captured.
- The phrase “695,026 Active Home Assistant Installations” is clearly presented as an analytics count, but the search snippet does not include the full surrounding page context beyond what is shown above.
